supportedTask: Supplementary fact base for house upgrade stardew: tier-by-tier and total budgets, practical direct unlocks/actions for each farmhouse upgrade tier, deficit wood budget example, and calendar/scheduling constraints.

facts.statement: Farmhouse upgrades at the Carpenter's Shop must be purchased in strict sequential order: Starter Farmhouse to Tier 1, Tier 1 to Tier 2, and Tier 2 to Tier 3 (Cellar). Players cannot skip an upgrade tier, nor can they order a subsequent upgrade while Robin is currently constructing an upgrade.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse 'Upgrades' table listing tiers 1, 2, 3 in progression; Carpenter's Shop 'House Upgrades' table showing successive upgrade requirements.
facts.appliesTo: All versions of Stardew Valley (1.6.15 current wiki revision).
facts.limitation: Does not apply to multiplayer cabins, which have their own independent upgrade track handled by farmhands.

facts.statement: The first farmhouse upgrade (Tier 1) costs 10,000g and 450 Wood, and Robin requires three days to construct it.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse 'Upgrades' table row 1: Cost '10,000g, Wood (450)'; Carpenter's Shop 'House Upgrades' table: Cost 10,000g, Ingredients 450 Wood, Build Time 3 Days.
facts.appliesTo: Stardew Valley 1.6+ (verified against wiki revision 15 January 2026).
facts.limitation: Only regular wood qualifies for the material requirement; hardwood cannot substitute.

facts.statement: Tier 1 farmhouse upgrade adds a kitchen equipped with a stove and a refrigerator (36 storage slots), expands the bedroom, and upgrades the bed from a single bed to a double bed, directly allowing marriage or Krobus to move in as a roommate.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse row 1 Changes: 'Adds a kitchen, with a kitchen counter that allows cooking, and a fridge that functions as a chest... Adds a bedroom. Upgrades bed from single to double. Allows marriage.' Cooking page: 'Cooking is a game mechanic that becomes available after upgrading the farmhouse for the first time.'
facts.limitation: Does not include advanced cooking recipes or roommate heart event mechanics; only the physical space and direct functional unlock.

facts.statement: The kitchen stove serves as the primary cooking interface. The refrigerator provides 36 slots of chest-like storage directly linked to the cooking interface, so ingredients stored inside the fridge (along with the player backpack inventory) are automatically accessible when cooking without manual transfer. In addition, the kitchen sink can refill the player's watering can.
facts.evidenceLocation: Cooking page: 'The stove is the cooking interface, while the refrigerator provides 36 slots of storage space... directly linked with the cooking interface, as if it were an extension of the player\'s inventory.' Farmhouse Notes: 'The kitchen sink can be used to refill the player\'s watering can.'
facts.limitation: Does not cover Mini-Fridge mechanics (purchased separately after Upgrade 1) or Cookout Kit.

facts.statement: The second farmhouse upgrade (Tier 2) costs 65,000g and 100 Hardwood, and Robin requires three days to construct it. In update 1.6, this cost was updated from the pre-1.6 price of 50,000g and 150 Hardwood.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse row 2: '65,000g, Hardwood (100)'; Version History 1.6 bullet: 'Raised price of second house upgrade (50,000g → 65,000g), but reduced number of hardwood needed (150 → 100).'; Carpenter's Shop 'House Upgrades' table row 2.
facts.limitation: Requires Tier 1 to be fully completed first. Pre-1.6 guides citing 50,000g and 150 Hardwood are outdated.

facts.statement: Tier 2 farmhouse upgrade enlarges both the kitchen and bedroom, and adds two new rooms: an empty room, and a nursery equipped with a crib and two child beds, directly enabling the player to have up to two children.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse row 2 Changes: 'Adds two new rooms, one empty, and one with a crib and two child beds, thus allowing the player to have children. Kitchen and bedroom are larger.'
facts.limitation: Does not cover detailed marriage dialogues, pregnancy trigger formulas, or child aging milestones.

facts.statement: Completing Tier 2 unlocks the 'House Renovations' catalog and exterior house/trim painting at the Carpenter's Shop. House renovations are executed instantly and can be undone for a full gold refund at any time, provided the renovation space is unoccupied.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse 'Renovations' section: 'After upgrading the farmhouse for the 2nd time, Robin offers house renovations. Renovations are completed instantly. All renovations can be refunded in full amount at any time, provided that the expanded area isn\'t occupied. Refunds also complete instantly.'
facts.limitation: Renovations are separate subsequent orders from the upgrade itself and require Tier 2 completed.

facts.statement: The third farmhouse upgrade (Tier 3 / Cellar) costs 100,000g and requires no wood or hardwood materials. Robin requires three days to construct it.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse row 3: '100,000g' (no materials listed); Carpenter's Shop row 3: Cost 100,000g, Ingredients None, Build Time 3 Days.
facts.limitation: Requires Tier 2 to be fully completed first.

facts.statement: Tier 3 adds an underground cellar beneath the farmhouse accessed via stairs in the kitchen, while the exterior footprint remains unchanged at 9x5. The cellar comes pre-equipped with 33 Casks and unlocks the Cask crafting recipe (20 Wood, 1 Hardwood). Casks accept Beer, Cheese, Goat Cheese, Mead, Pale Ale, and Wine to age them up to Iridium quality (doubling value). Casks only age items when placed inside the cellar; casks placed outside the cellar will not accept items.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse row 3: 'Adds a cellar under the house, allowing access via the kitchen. The cellar houses casks which can age products such as cheese and wine... The cellar comes with 33 casks, though it may house as many as 189 casks.' Cask page: 'Recipe Source: Final Farmhouse upgrade... Ingredients: Wood (20), Hardwood (1)... Casks can be placed anywhere; however, they will only accept goods to refine if they are actually in the cellar.'
facts.limitation: Does not cover full 189-cask optimal packing layouts or cross-season aging schedules; focuses on the direct capability of the cellar.

facts.statement: Across all three upgrades, the exterior footprint of the farmhouse remains fixed at 9 tiles wide by 5 tiles high (9x5). Upgrades expand the interior dimensions and add underground space without changing outdoor farm placement or requiring outdoor clearing around the house.
facts.evidenceLocation: Carpenter's Shop Farm Buildings table: Farmhouse footprint listed as 9x5; Farmhouse page demonstrates tier 2 and tier 3 sharing the same exterior sprite dimensions.
facts.limitation: Does not apply to farm buildings (e.g. barns/coops) whose footprints differ between tiers.

facts.statement: Mathematical cumulative requirement from Starter Farmhouse to Tier 1: exactly 10,000g, 450 Wood, and 0 Hardwood.
facts.sourceTitle: Derived from Farmhouse upgrade tier 1 verified prices
facts.evidenceLocation: Calculation derived from Tier 1 base cost.
facts.limitation: Deductive arithmetic calculation; not a literal quote from the wiki.

facts.statement: Mathematical cumulative requirement from Starter Farmhouse to Tier 2: exactly 75,000g (10,000g + 65,000g), 450 Wood, and 100 Hardwood.
facts.sourceTitle: Derived from Farmhouse upgrade tier 1 and tier 2 verified prices
facts.evidenceLocation: Arithmetic sum of Tier 1 and Tier 2 requirements.
facts.limitation: Deductive arithmetic calculation; not a literal quote from the wiki.

facts.statement: Mathematical cumulative requirement from Starter Farmhouse to Tier 3 (fully upgraded): exactly 175,000g (10,000g + 65,000g + 100,000g), 450 Wood, and 100 Hardwood.
facts.sourceTitle: Derived from Farmhouse upgrade tiers 1, 2, and 3 verified prices
facts.evidenceLocation: Arithmetic sum of all three upgrade tiers.
facts.limitation: Deductive arithmetic calculation; not a literal quote from the wiki.

facts.statement: Concrete Year 1 deficit budget calculation for Tier 1: A player who already possesses 200 Wood needs 250 additional Wood to reach the 450 Wood requirement (450 - 200 = 250). At Robin's Year 1 price of 10g per wood, purchasing the 250 deficit wood costs 2,500g (250 × 10g). Adding Robin's 10,000g upgrade labor fee yields a total cash outlay of 12,500g. This budget strictly covers the upgrade fee and wood deficit; it does not include Copper Axe upgrade fees (2,000g + 5 Copper Bars), food/energy consumption for chopping, or hardwood preparation costs for Tier 2.
facts.formula: Deficit wood = 450 - 200 = 250 wood; Purchase cost = 250 × 10g = 2,500g; Total cash outlay = 10,000g (labor fee) + 2,500g (wood) = 12,500g.
facts.sourceTitle: Carpenter's Shop permanent stock pricing (Wood: Year 1 10g) & Farmhouse tier 1 requirements
facts.evidenceLocation: Carpenter's Shop Permanent Stock: Wood Year 1 10g; Farmhouse Upgrade 1: 10,000g, 450 Wood.
facts.appliesTo: Year 1 only (Year 2+ wood price increases to 50g per wood).
facts.limitation: Specific concrete scenario with 200 wood owned in Year 1; does not generalize across all inventory combinations or later years.

facts.statement: Robin requires three full days of construction work for each farmhouse upgrade tier. Across three upgrades, total construction labor time is 9 work days.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse 'Upgrades' section: 'Robin requires three days to complete each farmhouse upgrade.'; Carpenter's Shop 'House Upgrades' table: Build Time '3 Days' for tiers 1, 2, and 3.
facts.limitation: Specifies construction work duration per tier, not calendar schedule span.

facts.statement: The total of 9 construction days across three tiers cannot be interpreted as a guaranteed 9 consecutive calendar days. First, tiers are strictly sequential: Tier 2 cannot be purchased until Tier 1 is fully finished, and Tier 3 cannot be purchased until Tier 2 is fully finished. Second, Robin begins construction the day after a purchase is made. Third, Robin does not work on festival days, which delay construction by 1 day. Fourth, Robin's shop is closed on Tuesdays and closes early at 4:00pm on Fridays, which restricts the days a player can place orders. Fifth, players require in-game time to accumulate 100 Hardwood and total gold (75,000g / 100,000g) between tiers.
facts.evidenceLocation: Carpenter's Shop: 'She will begin construction the day after buildings are purchased, but she does not work on festival days... The shop is closed on Tuesdays... The shop closes at 4:00pm on Fridays'; Farmhouse: sequential upgrade table.
facts.limitation: Boundary constraint ruling out sequential calendar day assumptions.

facts.statement: During farmhouse construction, Robin stands outside the player's farmhouse working on the building; the wiki notes that players can speak to and gift Robin during farmhouse, coop, and barn upgrades as an exception to the general gifting lockout. However, regarding the Carpenter's Shop sales counter, the wiki states generally: 'The shop is closed all day any day that she is working on a job on the Farm.' No wiki documentation states that the sales counter remains open or staffed for purchasing materials or farm buildings while Robin is on the farm upgrading the farmhouse. Therefore, counter availability during farmhouse upgrades is unverified and must not be claimed as open.
facts.evidenceLocation: Carpenter's Shop: 'The shop is closed all day any day that she is working on a job on the Farm.'; Robin: 'Her shop will be closed for the days that she is on the Farm completing the construction... Note that Robin is unavailable for gifting during construction of most farm buildings. She is available during Farmhouse, Coop, and Barn upgrades'.
facts.appliesTo: Construction periods across all farmhouse upgrades.
facts.limitation: Unverified counter status during farmhouse upgrade work; marked explicitly as unverified/not documented.

facts.statement: Scope fence: The house upgrade fact base only documents the direct mechanical triggers provided by the physical space (Tier 1 double bed enables marriage/roommate move-in; Tier 2 crib and child beds enable having up to two children). It deliberately excludes full relationship guides, bachelor/bachelorette gift preferences, 10/14-heart events, pregnancy probability algorithms, child growth stages, dove dismissals, and roommate mechanics.
facts.sourceTitle: Project Task Specification & V7 Scope Fence
facts.evidenceLocation: Task prompt: 用途解释仅回答“升级后能做什么”，不展开完整婚姻育儿。
facts.limitation: Negative scope boundary to prevent topic drift.

facts.statement: Scope fence: The house upgrade fact base documents the unlock condition (Tier 2 completed), instant execution, and full gold refundability of renovations at Robin's shop. It deliberately excludes the full catalog of individual renovation dimensions, prices, and room-by-room layout variations (such as Attic, Southern Room, Corner Room Expansion, Dining Room Wall, Cubby).

facts.statement: Scope fence: The house upgrade fact base documents the basic functional utility of the Tier 3 cellar and casks (33 base casks, recipe unlocked, cellar-only aging of wine/cheese/beer/mead/pale ale up to iridium quality, 189 maximum cask capacity). It deliberately excludes multi-season wine ROI calculations, Starfruit vs Ancient Fruit optimization debates, and dense 189-cask pathless packing/hoe-harvesting walkthroughs.
